issues.legal_issue: A potential liability deductible from compensation must be considered when estimating the open-market value of the right to receive that compensation, even if the liability itself is not deductible from net wealth as a debt.
material_facts: The assessee held a right to compensation after the estate vested in the State.
Agricultural income-tax arrears remained outstanding and could be deducted from the compensation under the applicable land-reform law.
The possibility and amount of that deduction had not been finally determined or fully reflected in the compensation amount.
The wealth-tax authorities valued the compensation right without accounting for the potential deduction.
issues.conclusion: The possibility of deducting the agricultural income-tax dues was a factor that had to be considered in estimating the compensation right’s open-market value. The extent of its effect was a matter of quantification. The appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(m) of the Wealth Tax Act, 1957, net wealth is computed by first valuing assets and then deducting eligible debts; section 7(1) requires an asset other than cash to be valued at the price it would fetch in the open market. A factor that would deter a willing purchaser or reduce the price must be considered at the valuation stage, even when the related debt is excluded from deduction at the separate net-wealth stage. Section 4(c) of the Bihar Land Reforms Act, 1950, permitted specified arrears to be recovered by deduction from compensation. The Court also referred to Pandit Lakshmi Kant Jha v. Commissioner of Wealth-tax, Bihar and Orissa for the proposition that the right to receive compensation is an asset; it found Standard Mills Co. Ltd. v. Commissioner of Wealth-tax and Commissioner of Wealth-tax v. Purshottam N. Amersey not relevant to the issue.

rule.if: wealth_tax_assessment and compensation_right_valued and deduction_hazard_exists and hazard_not_already_resolved

predicates.wealth_tax_assessment: The proceeding concerns the computation of a person’s net wealth for wealth-tax purposes.
predicates.compensation_right_valued: The value being assessed includes a right to receive compensation.
predicates.deduction_hazard_exists: A liability may lawfully be recovered by deducting it from the compensation.
predicates.hazard_not_already_resolved: The liability has not been finally determined or already reflected in the compensation value.

issues.definition: When a compensation right is valued in a wealth-tax assessment and an unresolved liability may be deducted from the compensation, the valuation must account for that possibility.
